newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Optimism in Swedish economy increases - poll.
newsitem.headline: Optimism in Swedish economy increases - poll.

text.p: Sweden's business sector is becoming more optimistic about the nation's economy with one in three company leaders expecting a pickup in the coming year, pollster SKOP said on Tuesday.

SKOP's latest quarterly survey, carried out in September, found 36 percent of the 584 company leaders interviewed now believed the economic situation in Sweden would improve over the coming year from current levels.
This compared to SKOP's May and February surveys in which only 26 percent of companies saw the economy improving over the next 12 months.
The survey, carried out between September 10-30, found 23 percent of companies expected the economic scenario to worsen over the next 12 months.
This was a fall from the May survey when 29 percent of companies were pessimistic about the coming year and from February when 45 percent of companies were downbeat.

But SKOP said companies were still not as confident in the economy as last year when a December survey found 48 percent of company leaders expected the economy to improve and only 16 percent were pessimistic.
Despite the more optimistic view for the economy, most company leaders still expected levels of unemployment to increase over the next year.
A total 42 percent of companies in the September survey expected unemployment to rise over the next year down from 49 percent in May but up from 24 percent last December.
Only 17 percent foresaw unemployment falling compared to 13 percent in May and 28 percent last December.
